source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: UK Food Standards Agency FHRS/FHIS open data, the publisher's all-authorities English-language file fhrs/FHRS_All_en-GB.csv ('All local authorities (English language)' on the open-data page; 'The data is updated daily', no archive, so the snapshot is the download date 2026-10-28, Last-Modified 2026-10-28 02:27 GMT, 614,606 establishments per the page), single table, no joins; the CSV header is not documented on the open-data page; the file's header line (fhrs/FHRS_All_en-GB.csv, header line, read 2026-10-28; UTF-8 with a byte-order mark) is 'AddressLine1,AddressLine2,AddressLine3,AddressLine4,BusinessTypeID,FHRSID,BusinessName,BusinessType,ConfidenceInManagement,Hygiene,Latitude,LocalAuthorityBusinessID,LocalAuthorityCode,LocalAuthorityName,Longitude,NewRatingPending,PostCode,RatingDate,RatingKey,RatingValue,RightToReply,SchemeType,Structural', and the 22 attributes are 22 of these 23 columns spelled as in the header (FHRSID, LocalAuthorityBusinessID, LocalAuthorityCode, NewRatingPending and SchemeType as the open-data page writes them; RatingValue, RatingKey, BusinessTypeID, Longitude, Latitude after the guidance's 'Rating Value', 'Rating Key', 'FSA Business Type ID', 'Longitude', 'Latitude'; Hygiene, Structural, ConfidenceInManagement for the three scores; LocalAuthorityName for the authority's Name); the published file has no LocalAuthorityWebSite or LocalAuthorityEmailAddress column (the authority's Url and Email exist only in the authorities code list), so these two attributes and the FD LocalAuthorityCode -> LocalAuthorityWebSite, LocalAuthorityEmailAddress were dropped; the business-type, rating, scheme-type and authority code tables are documentation of the codes and are not joined; dropped: RightToReply (free text, the only header column not taken).

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/fhrs_open-data.html, section 'About the data': "The LocalAuthorityBusinessID is provided by the local authority and is unique for that particular local authority data but could also be used by other local authorities. The FHRSID is system-generated and is unique in the data. It is based on the LocalAuthorityBusinessID and the LocalAuthorityCode."
truth.justification: The local authority's business ID is unique within that authority's data, so together with the authority code it identifies the record (the FHRSID is derived from the pair); the documented recycling of business IDs happens over time, not within one daily snapshot.

truth.clause: e3/truth/docs/fresh2/fhrs_APIv1_guidance_april24.pdf, p. 28 (Scheme Types): "A local authority can only belong to one scheme. The scheme in which they participate is determined by the country in which the local authority is located."
truth.justification: A local authority belongs to exactly one scheme (FHRS or FHIS), so its code determines the scheme type of every establishment it publishes.
